finite_graph.strategy: route_finite_native3d (v0.1.3 production finite multi-hop router; three-dimensional geometric contract)

bounds.edge_upper_bound_derivation: node_upper_bound * (len(finite_straight_steps) + 4 * len(finite_turn_radius_steps)) + the number of validated port attachment edges really built (source + target); no hardcoded constant.  A canonical node generates at most one straight per straight step and at most one turn per (perpendicular axis direction, turn radius step) pair, and every port attachment edge is the successor of exactly one node.

source.note: the source pose IS the canonical pose of this node (the lattice is anchored at the source), so the port is the node itself and no attachment curve is needed

target.note: validated local attachment curves inside the generic attachment neighbourhood; no case-specific waypoint, height or route is supplied

finite_graph.edge_cache_scope: one search; keyed by node id + the geometry/constraint/cost fingerprint above, never shared across scenes

graph_reuse.cache_provenance: graph_cache_state is 'cold' for the graph this call constructed and 'warm' for a caller-supplied graph; successor_cache_hits is that graph's successor-cache hit counter, read after the search
graph_reuse.note: the graph is reused only when every contract field is equal; the comparison is by CONTENT (Scene is mutable), and a mismatch is refused before any search expansion

finite_graph.edge_check_timing_note: the per-edge continuous constraint checks are attributed to the phase that really performs them: port attachments are validated while the graph is CONSTRUCTED (edge_check_s_graph_build, inside graph_build_s) and canonical successors lazily during the search (edge_check_s_search, inside search_s).  edge_check_s is their sum for THIS call; graph_object_totals holds the graph object's lifetime totals, which a warm reuse inherits

graph_object_totals.note: lifetime totals of the FiniteGraph OBJECT; for the cold default branch they equal this call's numbers, for a warm reuse they include the earlier call(s)

assembled_endpoint_check.method: the FIRST and LAST primitive of the assembled path are evaluated at their own endpoints and compared with the source and target poses the caller passed; every junction is measured between the end pose of one primitive and the start pose of the next.  Achieved errors, not certified bounds.
assembled_endpoint_check.guarantee: ok=True means the returned curve really starts at the source pose (source tolerances), really ends on the target acceptance ball, and is C0/C1 continuous inside the C1 tolerances.  It is NOT a proof about any other point of the curve; the hard constraints of the whole curve are checked separately by constraints.checks.validate_segments.

no_optical_loss_model: this engine computes geometry only; no dB, no insertion loss and no crosstalk number is produced

pose_contract.contract: normalise a legal non-zero 3D direction, reject otherwise
pose_contract.production_semantics: identical to production Pose3D.from_dict: exactly 3 finite numbers for the position, exactly 3 finite numbers for the tangent, the tangent must be a non-zero direction whose norm exceeds the shared 1e-12 threshold (geometry.vec.unit default tol), and the stored tangent is the NORMALISED one; everything else (zero direction, NaN, +-Infinity, missing field, 2 or 4 components, non-numeric component) raises ValueError inside the validator and can never yield a verdict of 'pass'
pose_contract.note: both poses were read by read_pose_dict(), which normalises a legal non-zero 3D direction and raises ValueError for every malformed pose; an un-normalised dot product can never enter acos()

boundary.method: exact analytic coordinate extrema per segment (no chord error, no sampling)

obstacle_clearance.method: exact segment/segment and segment/AABB distance for lines; adaptive chord subdivision with an explicit sagitta bound inside its proven domain for arcs; a curve point inside the keep-out is a violation witness; sampled minima are upper bounds only

centerline_spacing.method: certified chord bounds for every kind combination (line/line, line/arc, arc/line, arc/arc); exact segment/segment distance with an exact-rational fallback for line/line pairs; both sagittas subtracted and the sagitta domain dphi <= pi enforced; sampled minima are upper bounds only

tangent_sources.note: the JSON tangents were normalised by read_pose_dict before any dot product; the reported angles are the true 3D angles between unit directions (POSE_CONTRACT)

finite_difference_cross_check.note: central difference at +-1e-3 um; agreement within the chord error 1e-3/R rad confirms the analytic tangents

source_pose_check.pose_contract: normalise a legal non-zero 3D direction, reject otherwise
source_pose_check.method: the path start is compared against the SOURCE pose with the source tolerances; the target acceptance ball is not reused; the source tangent is the NORMALISED JSON direction

target_pose_check.pose_contract: normalise a legal non-zero 3D direction, reject otherwise
target_pose_check.method: the path end is compared against the TARGET pose acceptance ball; the target tangent is the NORMALISED JSON direction, so a non-unit tangent cannot fake a smaller angle

certification.notes: pass = every check was certified safe; fail = a violation witness or a bound that proves the requirement is missed; uncertified = a check could not be decided inside the refinement cap, or the certification self check failed (never reported as pass)
